44249-detectives-inc-a-mystery-story-for.title: A Mystery Story for Boys
44249-detectives-inc-a-mystery-story-for.creator: William Heyliger
44249-detectives-inc-a-mystery-story-for.description: A book by William Heyliger. It is simple to remember the blocks and to remember also when to go right or left. In familiar territory people with eyesight do not look for the name of every street. The master directs his dog by oral commands of "right," "left" or "forward." But it is the dog that guides the master.

God said that Christ would be like a beautiful light showing them where to go.

47263-the-peaches-of-new-york.title: Peaches Of New York
47263-the-peaches-of-new-york.creator: Unknown
47263-the-peaches-of-new-york.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The present volume is the fifth in the plan of the New York Agricultural Experiment Station to make a more or less complete record of all of the different fruits grown in this region.

arxiv-1708-08058.title: Algebraic models of the Euclidean plane
arxiv-1708-08058.creator: Jérémy Blanc, Adrien Dubouloz
arxiv-1708-08058.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Jérémy Blanc, Adrien Dubouloz. We introduce a new invariant, the real ( ( logarithmic ) ) -Kodaira dimension, that allows to distinguish smooth real algebraic surfaces up to birational diffeomorphism. As an application, we construct infinite families of smooth rational real algebraic surfaces with trivial homology groups, whose real loci are diffeomorphic to R 2 \mathbb{R}^{2} , but which are pairwise not birationally diffeomorphic. There are thus infinitely many non-trivial models of the euclidean plane, contrary to the compact case.

arxiv-2106-08855.title: Beyond Tikhonov: Faster Learning with Self-Concordant Losses via Iterative Regularization Thanks: Inria, École normale supérieure, CNRS, PSL Research University, 75005 Paris, France Thanks: Inria, Univ. Grenoble Alpes, CNRS, Grenoble INP, LJK, 38000 Grenoble, France
arxiv-2106-08855.creator: Gaspard Beugnot, Julien Mairal, Alessandro Rudi
arxiv-2106-08855.description: Abstract The theory of spectral filtering is a remarkable tool to understand the statistical properties of learning with kernels. For least squares, it allows to derive various regularization schemes that yield faster convergence rates of the excess risk than with Tikhonov regularization.

arxiv-2110-13223.title: Identifying and Benchmarking Natural Out-of-Context Prediction Problems
arxiv-2110-13223.creator: David Madras, Richard Zemel
arxiv-2110-13223.description: Abstract Deep learning systems frequently fail at out-of-context (OOC) prediction, the problem of making reliable predictions on uncommon or unusual inputs or subgroups of the training distribution. To this end, a number of benchmarks for measuring OOC performance have recently been introduced.

arxiv-2207-01748.title: Analysis of the dynamics induced by a competition index in a heterogeneous population of plants: from an individual-based model to a macroscopic model
arxiv-2207-01748.creator: Antonin Della Noce, Paul-Henry Cournède
arxiv-2207-01748.description: Abstract Competition indices are models frequently used in ecology to account for the impact of density and resource distribution on the growth of a plant population. They allow to define simple individual-based models, by integrating information relatively easy to collect at the population scale, which are generalized to a macroscopic scale by mean-field limit arguments.

arxiv-2211-17214.title: Lifting to Parity Decision Trees Via Stifling
arxiv-2211-17214.creator: Arkadev Chattopadhyay, Nikhil S. Mande, Swagato Sanyal, Suhail Sherif
arxiv-2211-17214.description: Abstract We show that the deterministic decision tree complexity of a (partial) function or relation f f lifts to the deterministic parity decision tree (PDT) size complexity of the composed function/relation f ∘ g f\circ g as long as the gadget g g satisfies a property that we call stifling .

arxiv-2212-06260.title: Exploring the vacuum structure of gravitationally induced neutrino masses
arxiv-2212-06260.creator: Carlos Henrique de Lima, Daniel Stolarski
arxiv-2212-06260.description: Abstract In this work, we explore the proposed mechanism in which the gravitational θ \theta anomaly generates neutrino masses. We highlight that the leading renormalizable interactions of the neutrino condensate forbid the possibility of generating hierarchical masses consistent with observation. This conclusion still holds when Standard Model loop corrections are accounted for.

arxiv-2302-13682.title: A deep learning approach to the measurement of long-lived memory kernels from generalised Langevin dynamics
arxiv-2302-13682.creator: Max Kerr Winter, Ilian Pihlajamaa, Vincent E. Debets, Liesbeth M. C. Janssen
arxiv-2302-13682.description: Abstract Memory effects are ubiquitous in a wide variety of complex physical phenomena, ranging from glassy dynamics and metamaterials to climate models. The Generalised Langevin Equation (GLE) provides a rigorous way to describe memory effects via the so-called memory kernel in an integro-differential equation. However, the memory kernel is often unknown, and accurately predicting or measuring it via e.g.

arxiv-2305-17519.title: Closure Certificates Conference: 27th ACM International Conference on Hybrid Systems: Computation and Control; May 14–16, 2024; Hong Kong, Hong Kong 27th ACM International Conference on Hybrid Systems: Computation and Control (HSCC ’24), May 14–16, 2024, Hong Kong, Hong Kong DOI: 10.1145/3641513.365
arxiv-2305-17519.creator: Vishnu Murali, Ashutosh Trivedi, Majid Zamani
arxiv-2305-17519.description: Abstract . A barrier certificate , defined over the states of a dynamical system, is a real-valued function whose zero level set characterizes an inductively verifiable state invariant separating reachable states from unsafe ones. When combined with powerful decision procedures—such as sum-of-squares programming (SOS) or satisfiability-modulo-theory solvers (SMT)—barrier certificates enable an automated deductive verification approach to safety.

arxiv-2403-08723.title: Asymptotic polynomial approximation in the Bloch space
arxiv-2403-08723.creator: Adem Limani
arxiv-2403-08723.description: Abstract . We investigate asymptotic polynomial approximation for a class of weighted Bloch functions in the unit disc. Our main result is a structural theorem on asymptotic polynomial approximation in the unit disc, in the flavor of the classical Plessner Theorem on asymptotic values of meromorphic functions.

arxiv-2503-06904.title: On Brezis’ First Open Problem: A Complete Solution
arxiv-2503-06904.creator: Liming Sun, Jun-cheng Wei, Wen Yang
arxiv-2503-06904.description: Abstract . In 2023, H. Brezis [ 5 ] published a list of his “favorite open problems”, which he described as challenges he had “raised throughout his career and has resisted so far”. We provide a complete resolution to the first one–Open Problem 1.

arxiv-2507-16457.title: Exactness, Cohomology, and Uniqueness in First-Order Differential Equations
arxiv-2507-16457.creator: Hemanta Mandal
arxiv-2507-16457.description: Abstract . This paper investigates the relationship between the solvability of first-order differential equations and the topology of the underlying domain through the lens of de Rham cohomology . We analyze the conditions under which a closed 1-form associated with a first-order ODE admits a global potential, thereby reducing the problem to the exactness of differential forms.

pmc-10590119.title: Hypercontractile cardiac phenotype in mice overexpressing the regulatory subunit PR72 of protein phosphatase 2A
pmc-10590119.creator: Julius R. Herting, Jule H. König, Katarina Hadova, Alexander Heinick, Frank U. Müller, Paul Pauls, Matthias D. Seidl, Carolina Soppa, Uwe Kirchhefer
pmc-10590119.description: BackgroundThe activity, localization, and substrate specificity of the protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) heterotrimer are controlled by various regulatory B subunits. PR72 belongs to the B'' gene family and has been shown to be upregulated in human heart failure. However, little is known about the functions of PR72 in the myocardium.

pmc-10649141.title: A Review of Novel Oximetry Parameters for the Prediction of Cardiovascular Disease in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea
pmc-10649141.creator: Siying He, Peter A. Cistulli, Philip de Chazal
pmc-10649141.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is a sleep disorder with repetitive collapse of the upper airway during sleep, which leads to intermittent hypoxic events overnight, adverse neurocognitive, metabolic complications, and ultimately an increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). The standard diagnostic parameter for OSA, apnoea–hypopnoea index (AHI), is inadequate to predict CVD morbidity and mortality, because it focuses only on the frequency of apnoea and hypopnoea events, and fails to reveal other physiological information for the prediction of CVD events.

pmc-10655333.title: Implementation strategies for large scale quality improvement initiatives in primary care settings: a qualitative assessment
pmc-10655333.creator: Debora Goetz Goldberg, Constance Owens-Jasey, Sahar Haghighat, Sneha Kavalloor
pmc-10655333.description: Background and objectivesThe EvidenceNOW: Advancing Heart Health in Primary Care was designed to assist primary care practices in the US in implementing evidence-based practices in cardiovascular care and building capacity for quality improvement. EvidenceNOW, NCT03054090, was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov on 15/02/2017.

pmc-11363011.title: Methylamine Separations Enabled by Cooperative Ligand Insertion in Copper–Carboxylate Metal–Organic Frameworks
pmc-11363011.creator: Katerina
pmc-11363011.description: Monomethylamine (NH2CH3), dimethylamine (NH(CH3)2), and trimethylamine (N(CH3)3) are important chemical feedstocks that are produced industrially as an azeotropic mixture and must be separated using an energy-intensive thermal distillation. While solid adsorbents have been proposed as alternatives to distillation for separating various industrial gas mixtures, methylamine separations remain largely unexplored in this context.

pmc-11440509.title: Mechanochemical Polyoxometalate Super-Reduction with Lithium Metal
pmc-11440509.creator: Magda Pascual-Borràs, Elisabetta Arca, Hirofumi Yoshikawa, Thomas Penfold, Paul G. Waddell, R. John Errington
pmc-11440509.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this first systematic investigation of mechanochemical polyoxometalate (POM) reduction, (TBA)3[PMo12O40] was reacted with n equiv of lithium metal (n = 1–24) to generate PMo12/n products which were shown to be mixtures of electron-rich PMo12Lix species. FTIR analysis revealed the lengthening/weakening of terminal Mo=O bonds with increasing levels of reduction, while EXAFS spectra indicated the onset of Mo–Mo bond formation at n ∼ 8 and a significant structural change at n > 12.

pmc-11691866.title: OVER SIX TIMES INCREASED RISK OF SUICIDAL IDEATION IN FAMILY CAREGIVERS WITH HISTORY OF CHILDHOOD ABUSE: THE ROLE OF NEUROTICISM
pmc-11691866.creator: Felipe Jain, Paulina Gutierrez-Ramirez, Miranda Zea, Liliana Ramirez Gomez
pmc-11691866.description: Despite high reported rates of suicidal ideation (SI) in family caregivers of persons living with dementia, little is known about the relationship between SI and intergenerational trauma. Those with a history of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) such as neglect and abuse are known to have worse psychological coping skills and higher rates of mental disorders.

pmc-12430512.title: Biotechnological Test of Plant Growth-Promoting Bacteria Strains for Synthesis of Valorized Wastewater as Biofertilizer for Silvicultural Production of Holm Oak (Quercus ilex L.)
pmc-12430512.creator: Vanesa M Fernández-Pastrana, Daniel González-Reguero, Marina Robas-Mora, Diana Penalba-Iglesias, Pablo Alonso-Torreiro, Agustín Probanza, Pedro A Jiménez-Gómez, Won Kyong Cho
pmc-12430512.description: The degradation of Mediterranean forest ecosystems, such as holm oak forests, has intensified in recent decades due to climate change, forest fires, and deforestation, compromising the natural regeneration of the soil. In this context, it is essential to apply sustainable strategies to restore soil and promote plant growth, thus helping the regeneration of the ecosystem.

pmc-12734975.title: Gut Microbiota-Targeted Photobiomodulation Ameliorates Alzheimer’s Pathology via the Gut–Brain Axis: Comparable Efficacy to Transcranial Irradiation
pmc-12734975.creator: Shisheng Cao, Xinyu Shi, Yongqiang Chen, Tiaotiao Liu, Jiashen Hu, Xiaoxi Dong, Hongli Chen, Jianwu Dai, Huijuan Yin, Michael Doulberis
pmc-12734975.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a major neurodegenerative disorder with limited effective and affordable therapies. Photobiomodulation (PBM) offers a safe, non-invasive treatment strategy, yet conventional transcranial PBM (tc-PBM) is restricted by low skull penetration. To overcome this limitation, gut microbiota-targeted PBM (gm-PBM) has been proposed to modulate the gut–brain axis, though its efficacy and mechanisms remain unclear.

pmc-13326227.title: Descending Aorta Perforation During Transseptal Puncture for Left Atrial Appendage Closure
pmc-13326227.creator: Tommaso Bini, Stefania Quintiliani, Vladimir Makaloski, Roberto Galea, Lorenz Räber, Nicolas Brugger
pmc-13326227.description: BackgroundAortic root injury during transseptal puncture (TSP) is a rare but well-recognized complication. However, injury to the descending aorta has not previously been described in this context.Case SummaryA 57-year-old woman underwent left atrial appendage closure. During TSP using the VersaCross Connect radiofrequency-powered system and a 15-F steerable sheath, an unrecognized perforation of the descending aorta occurred.

pmc-13559173.title: A group‐based hands‐on seminar for teaching failure mode and effects analysis in CyberKnife stereotactic radiotherapy
pmc-13559173.creator: Hiroyuki Okamoto, Shie Nishioka, Takeshi Kamomae, Kohei Okawa, Souichi Kikuchi, Junji Suzuki
pmc-13559173.description: BackgroundRisk analysis is becoming increasingly important in advanced radiotherapy, as treatment workflows grow more complex and require multidisciplinary expertise. Although failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) has been recommended for risk‐based quality management, opportunities for users to practically learn and apply FMEA within CyberKnife® workflows remain limited.
